title: Lane work order
description: The delegable unit of this programme. A work order is what a writer agent receives INSTEAD of a conversation, so every field here exists because its absence has already cost the programme something: an unbounded write set, a model chosen without a reason, a substitution with no expected count, a verification that needed a build nobody could run while the build was red.

wave.description: Which wave this belongs to. Intent, not a derived figure.

batch.description: The parallel batch this lane runs in. Every work order sharing a batch string must pass write-set-intersection together — that is what the batch NAME is for.

row.description: The ledger row that bounds this lane: a family id from family-ledger.json, or a synthetic id from synthetic-rows.json. The bound is what makes writeSet checkable; a work order without one is a promise.

reason.description: WHY THIS MODEL, written by a human. §1.2 of the programme law: a lane that cannot complete this field is not ready to be delegated — it is missing its pre-pass. Boilerplate is rejected by the validator, not by taste.

prePassEvidence.description: Path to the value-parity pre-pass evidence across the three verticals. REQUIRED when name is 'sonnet': sonnet never receives work that merely looks mechanical, and the validator checks the file exists rather than trusting the sentence.

writeSet.description: Globs this lane may write. Must resolve inside the row's writeRoot minus writeExcludes. Negation is not accepted here — exclusion is a field.

writeExcludes.description: Regions carved out of the write set. A plain path excludes a subtree; a glob excludes a shape, which is the only way two lanes sharing a directory can be proven apart.

readSet.description: What the lane may read. Stated because a lane that reads nothing outside its own files cannot have checked a cross-vertical value, and a reviewer needs to know which it was.

editClass.description: The kind of edit permitted. It selects which other fields are mandatory, so it cannot be decorative.

substitutionTable.description: Exact old→new pairs with the count each is expected to change. The count is the mechanism: a substitution that lands a different number of times has found something the pre-pass did not, and the lane stops.

deathProof.description: Required when editClass is deletion-with-death-proof. A read count of zero is a FLOOR, not a proof, so the claim has to name what was scanned and what was excluded.

expectedDiffInvariants.description: What the diff must look like afterwards. filesSubsetOfWriteSet is a const because it is law, not a preference — the post-hoc containment check enforces it.

forbiddenOps.description: Operations this lane may not perform, named explicitly. Standing fences plus whatever this lane's shape makes tempting.

mandatorySentence.description: The verbatim sentence §2 requires in every lane brief. Byte-compared (after whitespace normalisation) against the law; a paraphrase is a failure.

verificationCommands.description: Build-free commands the lane runs itself. Must include the channel-wiring zero-delta gate. A command needing dist/ is rejected: the build has been red, and a verification nobody can run is not one.

findingsFile.description: Where out-of-scope observations go. Every such observation is a written finding, not an edit — so the file has to exist as a destination before the lane starts.

commitPathspecs.description: Exact pathspecs for `git commit -- <pathspec>`. Must lie inside the write set. `.` and `-A` are refused: in a shared tree they commit another agent's work.
